nodes.label: Soil health monitoring

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Life on land|Soil health management|Soil health monitoring_qna_000
nodes.label: Facts
nodes.question: When was the soil sampling conducted?
nodes.answer: The soil sampling was conducted in late summer of 2022.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Life on land|Soil health management|Soil health monitoring_qna_001
nodes.label: Science and tech
nodes.question: How has X-ray microtomography been used in relation to soil?
nodes.answer: X-ray microtomography has been used to determine the volume fraction and distribution of air-filled pores in soil to help predict N2O emissions.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Life on land|Soil health management|Soil health monitoring_qna_002
nodes.label: Science and tech
nodes.question: Which methods or tools are mentioned in relation to measuring conditions relevant to the study?
nodes.answer: X-ray CT and oxygen sensors are mentioned as relevant tools.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Life on land|Soil health management|Soil health monitoring_qna_003
nodes.label: Science and tech
nodes.question: Which soil property varies predictably across the soil profile?
nodes.answer: Soil temperature is the only property expected to vary predictably across the soil profile.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Life on land|Soil health management|Soil health monitoring_qna_004
nodes.label: Science and tech
nodes.question: What methods were used to quantify the anaerobic soil volume fraction in the study?
nodes.answer: Various experimental approaches, including meta-analyses and oxic and anoxic incubations, were utilized to quantify the anaerobic soil volume fraction.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Life on land|Soil health management|Soil health monitoring_qna_005
nodes.label: Science and tech
nodes.question: What type of studies have shown the relationship between oxygen dynamics and soil conditions?
nodes.answer: Numerous soil incubation studies under different temperatures, water contents, or external oxygen concentrations have shown this relationship.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Life on land|Soil health management|Soil health monitoring_qna_006
nodes.label: Science and tech
nodes.question: What method was used for precise sampling of soil material in the study?
nodes.answer: An X-ray computed tomography aided sampling strategy was used for precise sampling of soil material.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Life on land|Soil health management|Soil health monitoring_qna_007
nodes.label: Science and tech
nodes.question: What method was used to collect samples for the study?
nodes.answer: Microsamples were collected from two distinct soil sites, one near and one far from visible pores, based on X-ray CT scans.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Life on land|Soil health management|Soil health monitoring_qna_008
nodes.label: Science and tech
nodes.question: Which elements were measured in the soil at the Swift Current site?
nodes.answer: The elements measured in the soil at the Swift Current site include bulk density, organic carbon, mineral nitrogen, and Olsen phosphorus.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Life on land|Soil health management|Soil health monitoring_qna_009
nodes.label: Taxonomy
nodes.question: How does the soil composition at the Brooks site compare to the Swift Current site?
nodes.answer: The soil at the Brooks site is a sandy loam with 46% sand, 32% silt, and 22% clay, compared to the silt loam at Swift Current.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Life on land|Soil health management|Soil health monitoring_qna_010
nodes.label: Science and tech
nodes.question: What type of soil is present at the Swift Current site?
nodes.answer: The soil at the Swift Current site is a silt loam, consisting of 31% sand, 51% silt, and 18% clay.
